nodes.label: Audio-vision
nodes.description: A unique mode of perception engaged by film, television, and other audiovisual media, combining seeing and hearing into a unified experience.

nodes.label: Added value
nodes.description: The expressive and informative value with which a sound enriches a given image, giving the impression it naturally comes from what is seen.

nodes.label: Vococentrism / Verbocentrism
nodes.description: The tendency of film sound to privilege the human voice (specifically speech), centering attention on it above other sounds.

nodes.label: Synchresis
nodes.description: The spontaneous and irresistible mental fusion between a sound and a visual event when they occur simultaneously (Synchronism + Synthesis).

nodes.label: Point of synchronization
nodes.description: A salient moment of an audiovisual sequence where a sound event and a visual event meet in synchrony, acting as a focal point.

nodes.label: Acousmatic sound
nodes.description: Sounds one hears without seeing their originating cause. Creates mystery and tension (e.g., the Acousmêtre).

nodes.label: Visualized sound
nodes.description: Sound accompanied by the direct sight of its source or cause on the screen.

nodes.label: Onscreen sound
nodes.description: Sound whose source appears in the image and belongs to the diegesis (reality of the film).

nodes.label: Offscreen sound
nodes.description: Sound whose source is part of the diegesis but is currently outside the visual frame.

nodes.label: Nondiegetic sound
nodes.description: Sound whose source is external to the story world, such as background music or voiceover narration.

nodes.label: Elements of Auditory Setting
nodes.description: Intermittent sounds with a singular source that help define the space of the scene (e.g., a distant siren).

nodes.label: Mutism
nodes.description: The absence of vocal speech in a film or scene, used to heighten the perception of other sounds and silence.
